task: Real-runner trial of changed-only deploys, plus first-run fixes (MAP #19)

analysis.objective: Show on the user's own self-hosted runner on the Mac host that a merge (deploy to stage) and a release (deploy to prod) rerun only Changed Steps, and that the next deploy after a failed one reruns from the right Step. Also make a new repo's first runs explain themselves: its first PR's Branch run rebuilds every Step and goes green when stage has never run, and its very first push to main does not start adops-stage.
analysis.successDefinition: All of these hold. (1) Branch rule: when stage has no saved Step Fingerprints for a Pipeline, `adops run --branch` no longer raises StageNotRunError (src/adops/application/run_pipeline.py:174-178). Instead it rebuilds every Step of that Pipeline in its own br_<branch>__ schemas, defers nothing to stage, writes no stage fingerprints and no Reverse Sync rows (Reverse Sync still makes only a Preview), and succeeds. The Branch rule with saved fingerprints (defer unchanged Steps, rebuild from the first Changed Step) is unchanged. Unit tests pin both cases and coverage stays at 100% line+branch. (2) ADR-0006 gets a dated Clarification describing the new first-run rule. The adops-share Skill text in both src/adops/templates/demo and src/adops/templates/plain (.claude/skills/adops-share/SKILL.md, around line 100) no longer describes a refusal; it explains that a first Branch run rebuilds everything. Every user-facing mention of 'stage has no Step Fingerprints' is updated or removed (try-the-assistant.md, promotion.md, tests/unit/interface/test_run_command.py). (3) First push: the generated src/adops/templates/github/workflows/adops-stage.yml skips the repo's very first push to main (github.event.before equal to 40 zeros) and still deploys every later push. This is checked by the existing parse-the-generated-YAML workflow tests. The 'cancel and re-run' note in promotion.md (line ~259) is rewritten to match. (4) Partial failure: a unit test sets up a changed-only deploy in which a rerun Step fails after earlier Steps passed. It shows that the earlier Steps' fingerprints were saved and the failed Step's were not, that the Settings Marker and the seen Accepted-Change Record ids were not advanced, and that the next `plan_deploy` / `adops run --all --changed` reruns from the failed Step. No new Docker e2e case is added and the e2e job stays under its 20-minute limit. (5) A manual real-runner trial on the Mac host (no OrbStack VMs, free disk checked first, Postgres Warehouse) uses this horizon's adops build and covers four things. (a) A fresh repo's first push does not start adops-stage. (b) Its first PR gets a green Branch run. (c) merge -> stage and release -> prod each rerun only Changed Steps, printing 'unchanged in <env>' for the rest. (d) One deliberately failing deploy, followed by a fixed one that reruns from the failed Step. Results go in a dated row under 'Recorded trials' in docs/playbooks/promotion.md (and in run-stage-and-prod-on-a-mac.md where relevant). (6) The repo's unit gate passes (with ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN set), as do lint, types and the existing e2e.
assumptions: The h18 deploy rules are binding as they stand: new record -> full Pipeline, adops.yaml Settings Marker change -> every Pipeline, no Schedule -> full, no saved fingerprints -> full, else from the first Changed Step. Step Fingerprints are saved per Step only after its Checks pass. This horizon proves those rules and does not change them.

The Settings Marker is saved only after every Pipeline passed (src/adops/interface/run_command.py:320). Seen record ids are marked only after the Pipeline passes (run_pipeline.py:582). So the partial-failure behaviour is believed correct already and needs a pinning test, not a fix. If the test shows otherwise, fixing it is in scope.
'Stage has never run' means no saved Step Fingerprints for that Pipeline in stage. A partial set of saved fingerprints keeps the existing rule: a Step without a saved fingerprint counts as changed.
When nothing is deferred, a Branch run reads the real Source for its Sync Steps, as it already does today when a Sync Step changed. The BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError fail-fast still applies.

'Very first push' is detected from the push event (created: true or before = 40 zeros). A repo created on GitHub with a README and then pushed is not a first push and may still start adops-stage; promotion.md says so.
Skipping the first push means stage first runs on the first merge; before that, stage has no fingerprints, which the new Branch rule covers.
The trial uses a Postgres Warehouse, runs the runner with ./run.sh on the Mac host, and builds the Server image from a wheel of this horizon's adops, not from PyPI.
One Server per machine (h16): release -> prod happens after switching the Server's ADOPS_ENVIRONMENT.
The trial is the last phase and depends on the code phases; it is verified by the recorded results in the guide.
confirmed: first PR Branch run with no saved stage fingerprints rebuilds every Step (ADR-0006 clarification)
confirmed: adops-stage.yml skips the repo first push to main
confirmed: partial failure proven by a unit test plus one failing deploy in the trial; no new e2e case
confirmed: real-runner trial is the last phase, Mac host, recorded in the guide

confirmed: before a fingerprint-saving run (stage/prod, full or from-step) reruns Steps from index k on, it forgets their saved fingerprints, so a failed Step always counts as changed; this clarifies the h18 never-pruned decision (stale rows of removed Steps are still never pruned)
confirmed: just before a Step runs in stage/prod, it and every later Step are forgotten (gate heal, user-approved); nothing is forgotten until the run reaches a Step
confirmed: trial Project is created with adops init from the local wheel; trial repo is created empty; a skipped deploy job on first push counts as the pass
confirmed: a Transform-first Pipeline on a first Branch run still reads stage raw schema; documented, not fixed
confirmed: blockers MAP.md lists as already answered are marked resolved at memory write
risks: A first Branch run's full rebuild loads the full Source into br_<branch>__raw_<source> on the stage Warehouse; for a large Source that is slow and may hit the 30-minute lock or the MCP tool-call timeout. The Skill text should set that expectation.
The new Branch path must not save stage fingerprints, must not write Reverse Sync rows, and drop-branch must still remove exactly br_<branch>__ schemas. Tests must assert all three.

ADR-0006 and vision criterion 5 say Branch Environments 'rebuild only changed Steps + dependents'; the full first-run rebuild must be a dated Clarification (with nothing saved, every Step counts as changed), not a silent contradiction.

The github.event.before/created guard may misfire on force-push, a recreated main, or a repo whose first commit came from GitHub's web UI; YAML-parsing tests cannot prove GitHub behaviour, only the trial can.
Skipping the first push could hide a misconfiguration on a repo whose runner was set up beforehand; promotion.md must say stage first runs on the first merge.
Trial disk usage on the Mac host: measure free disk before building Server images.
The trial needs a fresh private GitHub repo, a self-hosted runner, a GitHub prod environment and the user's time; it can stall while code phases are done.
The deliberately failing deploy must fail in a Step after at least one passing Step (e.g. a failing dbt test after a Sync).
The open h17 scheduled-run-overlap question may surface in the trial; not in scope to fix.
Removing StageNotRunError requires updating every test and doc that references it, or gates fail.
outOfScope: Rollback command: this horizon only produces inputs for it.
New Docker e2e case for partial failure or the first-run Branch: user chose unit test + manual trial to protect the 20-minute e2e job.
Trial on OrbStack, Linux VMs or Docker Desktop: user said Mac host only.
DuckDB-Warehouse Server trial: DuckDB Servers must be Linux.
Changing the h18 deploy rerun rules: binding decisions; this horizon proves them.
Scheduled-run overlap and first-prod-deploy side effects (h17 blockers): observed if seen, not fixed.
Automatic drop-branch in CI, fork-PR policy: earlier deferred decisions.
A prod approval step for private repos without Enterprise (h8 blocker).
Publishing a new adops release to PyPI: the trial uses a locally built wheel.
Upgrade path for existing Projects' generated workflows and Skills: MAP #24.
analysis.domainShapeReason: The parts that matter change and prove DataOps rules a data engineer recognizes: the Branch Environment first-run rule (ADR-0006), how Promotion deploys pick Changed Steps by Step Fingerprint, and how a failed deploy resumes.

ubiquitousLanguage.meaning: A Step whose Step Fingerprint differs from the one saved by the Environment's last successful run (or has none), so it and later Steps rerun.
Hash of a Step's definition, saved per Step only after its Checks pass, only in stage and prod, never by a Branch run.
`adops run --branch` for a PR, building in br_<branch>__ schemas; defers unchanged Steps to stage, or rebuilds every Step when stage has never run that Pipeline.
A new repo's first push and first PR, when no runner or Server folder may exist yet and stage has no saved Step Fingerprints.
`adops run --all --changed` in the stage and prod workflows, rerunning only Changed Steps and printing 'unchanged in <env>' for the rest.
A changed-only deploy in which a rerun Step fails after earlier Steps passed; the next deploy must rerun from the failed Step.
The manual, dated test of Promotion on the user's self-hosted runner on the Mac host, recorded under Recorded trials in the playbook.
An Environment's Settings Marker and seen Accepted-Change Record ids in adops._adops_deploy_state, advanced only when the deploy succeeds.

phases.name: Change first Branch run to rebuild every Step
phases.goal: When stage has no saved Step Fingerprints for a Pipeline, a Branch run (`adops run --branch`, which builds a pull request's work in its own br_<branch>__ Warehouse schemas) rebuilds every Step of that Pipeline and succeeds, instead of refusing with StageNotRunError. Every user-facing text that described the refusal now describes the rebuild.
phases.rationale: A new repo's first pull request runs before stage has ever deployed, so today its Branch run always fails with 'stage has no Step Fingerprints'. Discovery showed the domain already handles an empty stage (first_changed_step returns 0, so every Step counts as changed), so the work is removing the guard and fixing the tests and texts that mention it. This is one small slice across layers: the application rule, the CLI error mapping, tests and docs, about 9 files, and no other phase consumes its pieces.
changes: Delete the StageNotRunError class (run_pipeline.py:174-178) and its raise in plan_branch_run (run_pipeline.py:644-655), so an empty fingerprinting.store.load(pipeline.name) builds BranchRun(env, {}, first) with first = 0 and nothing deferred to stage.
Remove StageNotRunError from the import (run_command.py:35) and from RUN_ERRORS (run_command.py:102-109); the MCP server and Server use RUN_ERRORS and need no code change.
Change the `adops run` docstring (run_command.py:271-272) so --help says --branch rebuilds the Steps that differ from stage's last successful run, or every Step when stage has never run the Pipeline.

Replace the refusal test in test_run_pipeline.py (:71 import, :1725-1729) with a first-run test: empty stage fingerprints -> every Step PASSED (none DEFERRED), no fingerprint saved, Reverse Sync applied nothing and produced a Preview, only br_<branch>__ schemas written.
Keep a test pinning that BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError (the fail-fast when dbt sources do not read the branch's raw schema) still fires on a first-run Branch with empty stage fingerprints.
Replace the CLI refusal test (test_run_command.py:1159-1166) with one asserting the printed first-run output, and assert the Run Log text equals that printed output (shared result_lines).
Replace the MCP refusal test (test_mcp_server.py:477-482) with one asserting the tool call succeeds with every Step rebuilt.

Append a dated '## Clarification (2026-11-28)' section to ADR-0006 (do not edit the original text): with no saved stage fingerprints every Step counts as changed, so the first Branch run rebuilds the whole Pipeline from the real Source; a Pipeline whose first Step is a Transform still reads stage's raw_<source> schema, which may not exist yet.

Rewrite the refusal paragraph in BOTH adops-share SKILL.md files (around lines 100-105) with byte-identical text: a first Branch run rebuilds every Step and may take as long as loading the full Source.
Rewrite docs/try-the-assistant.md:94-96 to describe the first-run rebuild instead of the refusal.
Run the unit gate with ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN=postgresql://postgres:adops@localhost:55432/postgres and confirm 100% line+branch coverage, plus ruff and types.

rubric.label: Empty-stage Branch run rebuilds every Step
rubric.ruleStatement: A Branch run of a Pipeline with no saved stage Step Fingerprints runs every Step in br_<branch>__ schemas, defers none to stage, saves no fingerprint and succeeds.
passCriteria: `grep -rn StageNotRunError src/ tests/` returns nothing.
A test in tests/unit/application/test_run_pipeline.py starts a Branch run with an empty fingerprint store and asserts every Step result is PASSED and none is DEFERRED.
The same test asserts the fingerprint store is still empty after the run, Reverse Sync applied nothing and produced a Preview, and every Warehouse write went to a br_<branch>__ schema.
`ADOPS_TEST_POSTGRES_DSN=postgresql://postgres:adops@localhost:55432/postgres uv run pytest tests/unit/application/test_run_pipeline.py -k branch` passes.
Score 10 only if the test also uses a Pipeline with at least one Sync Step and one Transform Step and asserts the Sync Step read the real Source (not a stage schema).
failureExamples: The raise is removed, but the new test only checks the run did not raise and never asserts that no Step was DEFERRED or that no fingerprint was saved.
StageNotRunError is caught in run_command.py and turned into a warning, so the application still refuses and the CLI prints a softened error.
A Branch run with an empty store saves fingerprints because the empty case goes down the stage path.

rubric.label: Existing Branch rules still hold
rubric.ruleStatement: Removing the guard does not weaken the BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError fail-fast or the rule that a partial set of stage fingerprints defers only the unchanged prefix.
passCriteria: A test in test_run_pipeline.py asserts BranchSourcesNotParameterizedError is raised for a first-run Branch (empty stage fingerprints) whose dbt sources do not read the branch's raw schema.

The existing tests for a Branch run with a partial or full set of stage fingerprints (deferring unchanged Steps) still pass without changes to what they assert: `git diff tests/unit/application/test_run_pipeline.py` shows no removed DEFERRED assertions outside the replaced refusal test.
failureExamples: The fail-fast check sat after the deleted guard and was removed with it, so a first Branch run silently reads stage's raw schema.
The refusal test is deleted and replaced, but an unrelated deferral test is also loosened to make the suite pass.

rubric.label: CLI and MCP show the rebuild
rubric.ruleStatement: `adops run --branch` and the MCP run tool both succeed on an empty stage and report every Step rebuilt; the Run Log text matches the printed output; --help describes the first-run rebuild.
passCriteria: A test in tests/unit/interface/test_run_command.py runs `adops run --branch` on an empty stage, asserts exit code 0 and one rebuilt line per Step, and asserts the Run Log text equals the printed text.
A test in tests/unit/interface/test_mcp_server.py asserts the run tool call returns success with every Step rebuilt, not an error.
`uv run adops run --help` mentions that --branch rebuilds every Step when stage has never run the Pipeline.
`grep -n StageNotRunError src/adops/interface/run_command.py` returns nothing.
failureExamples: The CLI test asserts only exit code 0 and never compares the Run Log with the printed output.
The MCP refusal test is deleted rather than replaced, so nothing pins MCP behaviour on an empty stage.
The --help docstring still says --branch needs stage to have run.

phases.name: Change deploys to forget fingerprints before rerunning Steps
phases.goal: In a run that saves Step Fingerprints (a stage or prod run, either full or a Changed-only deploy rerunning from Step k), just before each Step runs it forgets (deletes) the saved fingerprints of that Step and every later Step, and saves the new one only after its Checks pass. So after a failure the saved fingerprints are exactly the Steps that passed, still in Step order, and the next deploy (and any Branch run) reruns exactly from the failed Step.
phases.rationale: Discovery found a Partial failure bug: a failed Step keeps its old saved fingerprint, so the next deploy can wrongly treat it as unchanged (the in-memory fakes skip it; the real Warehouse store reruns from an earlier Step only by an accident of row ordering). The user decided the fix: just before a Step runs, forget it and every later Step. Forgetting only the one Step would not work, because the real store gives a re-saved row the next saved_order and Steps are compared by position, so the saved order would be shuffled after a failure. This is one small slice across layers: one new port method, its Warehouse adapter and two fakes, one wiring call in run_pipeline and the tests, with no piece consumed by another phase.

phases.rationale: Unit tests and YAML parsing cannot prove how GitHub fires the push event or how a real runner and Server behave, so the user asked for a manual trial as the last phase. It is executed by hand by the user with the executor guiding, and its rubric is the recorded results.
